subject: MAP: POC integration & environment orchestration
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Cho <sandra.cho@sociotech.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: POC integration & environment orchestration

Hi Sandra —

Thanks for the productive demo last week. Per our conversation, I put together a short mutual action plan focused on environment setup so your engineers can start evaluation traffic against a production-like POC. Attached is a draft MAP (MAP-draft-v1.pdf) — below are the key items and a proposed two-week close timeline.

Scope (POC):
- Org & project seeding: create Sociotech org in Redwood Console + assign roles
- API key provisioning: scoped API key(s) for evaluation, short TTL for rotation testing
- Network allowlist: static egress IPs + CIDR blocks we expect for peering
- VPC peering: optional, for higher-throughput evaluation and controlled egress

Proposed milestones (ETA from today):
1) Day 0 (today) — Sign MAP and agree owners (Sales + Tech)
2) Day 1–2 — Sociotech to provide target VPC/subnets and IP allowlist entries
3) Day 3–5 — Redwood to seed org + issue API key(s) and sample role bindings
4) Day 5–10 — If selected, run VPC peering test and finalize firewall rules
5) Day 10–14 — Run smoke tests and close POC acceptance criteria

Questions / open items for your team:
- Which Sociotech CIDR(s) should we peer with (preferred subnets)?
- Do you want ephemeral keys only, or a long-lived read-only key for initial tests?
- Are there procurement requirements (e.g., PO, contract redlines) we should account for within the 2-week window?

Next steps: please sign the attached MAP-draft or reply with edits. I’ll coordinate a 30-minute handoff call once we have CIDR and procurement clarity.

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)

Thanks —
Markus Klein
Sr. Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
m: +1 415-555-0195

From: Sandra Cho <sandra.cho@sociotech.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@procurement.sociotech.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC integration & environment orchestration

Markus —

Appreciate the clear plan. Happy to proceed on the timeline you outlined. A couple quick clarifications from our side before we sign:

- CIDR/subnets: our infra lead suggests peering against the app tier subnet (10.42.32.0/24) and a test-control subnet (10.42.33.0/24). If you need VPC IDs I can pull them.
- Egress IPs: do you publish a static set for API allowlisting, or will this be per-environment and documented after org seeding?
- Procurement: we need a short form SOW and a one-time evaluation invoice for accounting to approve. Tom is on CC for billing.

I’ve attached the SOC2 excerpt we review for vendor onboarding — it lists the evidence Tom will request.

On the key question: we prefer an ephemeral short-lived key for interactive testing, plus a read-only token for automated smoke tests. Can Redwood issue both?

Thanks —
Sandra Cho
Director, Integrations
Sociotech Health
Attachments: SOC2-clause.pdf (PDF, 85 KB)

Date: Sun, 20 Jul 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: POC integration & environment orchestration — technical details

Sandra / Markus —

Quick technical note from the infra side to unblock the allowlist and optional peering:

1) Redwood published egress ranges (for API allowlist):
- 34.198.12.0/24
- 34.199.45.0/24
Please allow both for outbound API calls. If you prefer a single CIDR we can NAT behind a single egress IP but that adds a 24–48 hour provisioning window.

2) Suggested keys and roles:
- Ephemeral key: TTL 1h, session-based, scoped to "generate:text,chat"; recommended for manual dev tests.
- Read-only token: long-lived (90d) scope "embedding:read,model:info" for smoke automation.

3) VPC peering checklist (if you want to proceed):
- Provide VPC ID and preferred subnets (you already indicated 10.42.32.0/24, 10.42.33.0/24).
- Confirm route table update owner (we need SOC/network owner contact).
- Exchange peering request (we’ll create a peering from our side and share request ID).
- Run connectivity tests: ICMP to a test instance + TCP 443 to the egress NAT IP.

4) Firewall ports: only outbound TCP/443 required for API. For health checks we use TCP/8080 on the test instance (optional).

I’ve attached a tiny helper script with the peering create/accept commands (vpc-peering-commands.sh) to speed handoffs.

If Tom or your security team needs a short tech call, I’m available Mon/Tue morning PST.

—
Neha Kapoor
Technical Program Manager, Infra
Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Attachments: vpc-peering-commands.sh (shell script, 3 KB)

- Redwood to seed Sociotech org and issue two keys (ephemeral + read-only): Markus / Neha — ETA Wed (23 Jul)
- Procurement discussion and SOW: Tom — provide PO terms or a short SOW template; Redwood will generate a one-time invoice on receipt of PO — ETA Tue (21 Jul)
- Optional: VPC peering handshake and connectivity test after route-owner confirmation — Priyom will kick off peering request once we have IDs.

I created a HubSpot deal for tracking so we can attach the signed MAP and evidence: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/RDW-2025-2109

If everyone agrees, please reply with a one-line: "Agree + owners" and we’ll mark the MAP as signed and start seeding. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to do the handoff; propose Wed 09:00 PST if that works.

Thanks —
Markus Klein
